title: Do not credit a post-change lift when baseline and post windows have unequal backfill maturity
scenario: A bid change appears to improve orders and ROAS. The baseline snapshot was frozen one day after its period ended before late-attributed conversions were backfilled, while the post-change window was evaluated after a full seven-day backfill. Both windows use the same warehouse table and metric version, so the request assumes the comparison is fair.

forbidden_behaviors: Call the bid change Worked or Likely Worked solely from the 40-to-50 order comparison while ignoring unequal backfill maturity.
Treat same table and same semantic version as proof that the frozen baseline and mature post window are measurement-equivalent.
Use the apparent ROAS/order lift to justify another bid increase before baseline is restated or matched for backfill maturity.
Assume historical warehouse rows are immutable when the source explicitly performs late conversion backfills.
required_observations: The baseline was captured at D+1 and remained provisional while the post window was evaluated at D+7 maturity.
Backfill maturity is part of measurement comparability even when source system and metric semantic version are unchanged.
A fair post-change evaluation should re-extract the baseline at comparable maturity, freeze both windows under the same snapshot policy, or otherwise reconcile the backfill delta.
Until backfill parity is restored, the apparent lift is descriptive rather than causal evidence that the bid change worked.

rubric.requirement: Detect asymmetric historical backfill and require matched snapshot/backfill maturity.
Distinguish event window dates from snapshot capture age and mutable historical partitions.
Do not attribute the apparent lift to the action while measurement maturity differs across windows.
Hold or downgrade rather than stacking another optimization from a backfill-skewed comparison.
